trickyParts: Delivery from commit needs the commit time of the inserting transaction; events rows are updated by the outbox (published_at), so commit-trigger.sql copies marked events into loadtest.event_commits inside the inserting transaction and pg_xact_commit_timestamp(xmin) is read from there (track_commit_timestamp on at initdb).
Committed is counted from loadtest.event_commits, not HTTP status: at 1x 356-378 writes hit the 30 s client timeout but many committed and still get delivery latencies.

The guard sends the listener a wrong token too: a listener with no ENVOY_API_TOKEN accepts every caller (cmd/listener/apiauth.go:37-56), so 2xx with the stack token alone would not prove it is the stack's listener.

Every stack process runs under env -i: the pod's DISPATCH_URL, ENVOY_URL, ENVOY_NATS_URL, AWS_* and HOME never reach Dispatch, which would otherwise read $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/legion/envoy.json and call Bedrock. Processes are stopped only by pidfile pid after checking /proc/<pid>/exe.
deviations: stack.sh has extra subcommands reset, loadgen, build-info, stop NAME..., seed --force so run-step.sh and run-series.sh share one implementation; README lists them.
Dispatch's signing key lives under the stack's HOME instead of DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY; Dispatch is stopped at the end of each step so the box is idle between steps.
Route names use the full template ('browser GET /api/v1/issues/{key}'), as the plan's format says, not the archive's short names.
loadgen tables takes -tops=false; run-series.sh uses it for the combined table, since each step already rendered its pprof tops.
discoveredComplexity: At 10x on the 2-vCPU pod most requests and writes fail with 'dial tcp: i/o timeout' after 5 s. A second 10x run with a side monitor showed curl from another process also failed to connect while ~3,200 connections sat in SYN_SENT, recovering when the generators stopped: new connections to Dispatch's port stop being accepted on the box. README 'Connect timeouts above 1x' records it; dispatch://INFRA-592 (refuse excess load instead of collapsing) is the tree's issue for that behaviour.
